title: docs(gate): the eager-closure gate's prose stops writing counts it cannot keep
body:
Fixes #7528

## The deliverable is "stop writing the count", not "52 becomes 50"

Three sentences described the aggregate as *"one number over **52** chunks"*. The
card's diagnosis is the whole design brief: the count is **not load-bearing for
any verdict** — the sentence is rhetorical (*"one total over N chunks cannot say
WHERE the payload moved"*) — which is exactly why nothing ever caught it. And
today there were **three** different counts in play, so refreshing one literal
would have turned three into two and let the next build spread them again.

Each sentence now states its population and leaves the figure to the gate, which
prints it on every run. The checker's header carries the rule, generalised from
the one that file already applies to its own motivating table:

> That table is the MOTIVATING measurement and stays pinned to `77f846a8b`; it is
> not the current reading.

An **anchored** count is a measurement of a named build and cannot go stale; an
**unanchored** one is a standing claim about the live closure, which moves on most
builds. That is also the distinction the card used to leave
`vite-declared-lazy-views.ts`'s "42.5 KB of headroom" alone — it sits in a
paragraph dated to a `b98352a15` measurement and reads as history.

## The numbers, measured on this branch, not copied from the card

⚠️ A full `pnpm turbo run build --filter='./packages/*'` plus
`pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` on `52cac3886`, then
`pnpm check:eager-closure`:

| reading | card said | measured here |
|:--|--:|--:|
| the gate's live verdict line | 50 of 518 | `across **50 of 518** chunks` |
| the prose | 52 | 52 |
| the file's own `BASELINE.chunks` | 48 | 48 |
| eager closure, gzipped | 3,258,288 B (on `f620a26f6`) | **3,263,896 B** |

The three counts confirmed; the payload has grown 5,608 bytes since the card was
written. `BASELINE.chunks` is **not** a fourth defect and is untouched: it names
the commit it was measured on (`3d257c85a`), which is the anchored form the rule
asks for.

## Site 2 — the workflow cited a ceiling that no longer exists

⚠️ Not a drifted number: `3.15 MB` is 3,300,000 bytes, the ceiling objectui#6683
set and **objectui#6776 retired**. Established on today's tree before rewriting,
rather than assumed: the criterion actually in force is
`MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES = 3_268_000` (3.12 MiB), plus the objectui#5924
sensitivity half that weighs each ceiling against the report it just read. So a
sentence whose entire purpose is to stop a reader concluding the payload is
acceptable was itself quoting a size the gate had not allowed for two
re-baselines.

The repair names **no size at all** — which is the rule the same paragraph already
applies to the ceiling itself (*"The closure ceiling is NOT set here. It lives in
`scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` next to the reasoning that produced
it"*), now applied to the ceiling's value too. The removed literal is not quoted
back, for the same reason the pin refuses quotations.

## The pin

One `it.each` in the gate's own test file — one gate, one home. It fails when a
numeral qualifies a chunk noun in either script's prose **and no commit in its
window anchors it**, so the class fails loudly rather than waiting to be read.

Deliberately narrow, each limit a decision: numerals qualifying a **chunk** noun
(the file's "144 modules" and "166 modules" are module counts inside anchored
change records); own-line comments; and an anchor window of a paragraph plus the
one before it, because the header writes "Measured on `77f846a8b`:" as a lead-in
and its table as a separate paragraph. A line of **code** breaks that window, so a
hash in one block never vouches for a count in another. The window errs toward
allowing, which is the tolerable side for a check on prose; the intolerable side
is a standing claim nobody refuses.

⚠️ It also means this diff may not quote its own old literals back — the pin
cannot tell a quotation from a claim. That is recorded in the docblock, and it is
why the prose above says "N" where the number used to be.

## Ablation — three legs, and the sharp one is (b)

**(a) The genuine pre-fix prose**, pin retained. Both files went red, each naming
itself and the exact literals:

```
× check-eager-closure-budget.mjs writes no chunk count that no commit anchors
AssertionError: check-eager-closure-budget.mjs states a chunk count (52 chunks, 52 chunks) that names no commit …
  expected [ '52 chunks', '52 chunks' ] to deeply equal []
AssertionError: check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts states a chunk count (52 chunks) …
Tests  2 failed | 99 passed (101)
```

**(b) A literal that is CORRECT TODAY** — the leg that proves the pin governs the
class of writing rather than wrong numbers. `50 chunks` and `50 of 518 chunks` are
exactly what the gate printed an hour earlier, and both are still refused:

```
expected [ '50 chunks' ] to deeply equal []
expected [ '50 of 518 chunks' ] to deeply equal []
Tests  2 failed | 99 passed (101)
```

**(c) The same today-correct count, ANCHORED** — "Measured on `52cac3886`, the
closure held 50 of 518 chunks" — is **accepted** (`101 passed`). So the pin is not
"no digits near chunks"; it is the anchoring rule, and the escape hatch its own
failure message offers actually works.

Ordering, and it is the reason all three legs are trustworthy: the implementation
was **committed first**, and only then was the restore `trap` armed — the sibling
seat on objectui#7448 had its trap fire on a precondition guard's own exit and
silently restore both files to a HEAD that did not contain the fix. Each leg
re-checked that HEAD carried the fix *before* arming (`exit 92` if not). Mutation
proven on disk each time (blob hash flip plus an injected-anchor count) before
running; restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`; restoration proven
**by state** — `git diff HEAD` empty, porcelain empty, both blobs back to their
HEAD hashes. No build or `dist/` is on this path: the pin reads the checkout.

⚠️ The pin's own self-test caught a real bug in the matcher during development —
a hash in one comment block anchored a count in the next block across a line of
code. That is why `proseLines` distinguishes a blank comment line from code, and
why the self-test asserts that case.

## Verification, all on `8537eb4b4`

| check | result |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__` (whole dir) | `Test Files 104 passed (104)` · `Tests 3065 passed (3065)` |
| `pnpm run type-check:scripts` | exit 0; `--listFiles` confirms **both** edited script files are in the program |
| `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` | `✅ Console eager closure is 3187.4 KB gzipped across 50 of 518 chunks (budget: 3191.4 KB, headroom: 4.0 KB).` |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 6365 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --self-test` | `OK check-governed-queue-guard self-test: 132 cases pass` |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test .github/workflows/performance-budget.yml` | `✅ NOT GOVERNED — 1 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched.` |
| `node scripts/check-shell-escape-residue.mjs` | `✅ check-shell-escape-residue: OK` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `✅ No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` — acted on: none added |
| control-byte self-scan over all three edited files | no match |

Every gate's own verdict line, with the exit code captured by redirecting to a
file first — never read through a pipe.

**ESLint, narrowed and the narrowing proven** (repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run):
the two edited script files lint clean — `--format json` reports 2 files, 0 errors,
0 warnings. The workflow is outside ESLint's population entirely: asked with the
repo's own config it answers *"File ignored because no matching configuration was
supplied."* And the config enables no type-aware linting
(`js.configs.recommended` + `tseslint.configs.recommended`, no
`parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot move the verdict
on any untouched file.

## Scope

Clause-② stayed **`no`** — no predicate, no scan population, no verdict, no
constant. Comments in three files, plus four `it` cases in the gate's existing
test file. The prose was checked against the gate's **behaviour**, not only its
count, and it was right about behaviour: the aggregate really is one number over
the whole closure and really cannot localise a regression, which is why
`PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS` exists. objectui#7518's aggregate-headroom sentences
were **not** touched.

Also folded in, exactly as the card and its triage ruled — a clarifying sentence,
deleting neither figure: the header names both `3.07 MB` and `3.12 MB` in one
paragraph without saying which is which. They are `BASELINE`'s measured payload
and `MAX_EAGER_CLOSURE_GZIP_BYTES` rendered in MiB; the note now says so.

**Out of scope, filed unassigned** after a REST dedup over the `finding` and
`domain:devx` label listings paged to exhaustion (203 unique open issues) with
#7528 as a known-hit control:

- **#7848** — ⚠️ the live aggregate headroom is **4.0 KB (0.05x** the 89 KB
  regression the gate must catch**)** where the file's own design argument assumes
  45.7 KB. `Bundle Analysis` is a required context, so the next ~4 KB of eager
  closure lands red on `main`. Not a ceiling-raise request; the two honest routes
  (find the bytes, or a declared re-baseline) are the maintainer's call.
- **#7850** — `performance-budget.yml`'s prose carries no pin of this shape, and
  the two obstacles to extending it are named there.

Neither is addressed here; both remain open.
